content.heading: Documentation Reference Standard
content.purpose: Govern how KIS documentation uses canonical KIS authority, normative protocol sources, prescriptive writing guidance, implementation references, and inferred evidence without creating duplicate fact ownership.

authority_model.domain: KIS-specific facts, behavior, policy, configuration, lifecycle, and adopted requirements
The bounded conformance domain owned by the external standard
Presentation or practice guidance where KIS authority is silent
Bounded reusable documentation or engineering patterns
Derived evidence requiring verification against an owning source

output_classes.purpose: Teach concepts, tasks, workflows, examples, architecture, and operations in reader-oriented prose.
output_classes.source_rule: Canonical KIS facts supply factual content; approved references may inform organization and presentation only.

output_classes.purpose: Explain adopted normative behavior while preserving requirement strength, identifiers, ownership, and traceability.
output_classes.source_rule: Adopted KIS MRDs and applicable normative external standards supply requirements; generated prose remains non-authoritative.

output_classes.purpose: Expose exact tools, schemas, settings, policies, states, relationships, capabilities, permissions, and provenance.
output_classes.source_rule: Only canonical KIS facts or explicitly applicable normative protocol facts may populate factual reference data.

registry_contract.relationship: semantic registry references acquisition identities; it does not duplicate acquisition configuration

requirements.statement: Every admitted documentation reference MUST declare one source role, bounded permitted uses, provenance, freshness strategy, lifecycle state, and authority limit.
KIS-owned factual content MUST remain sourced from its current canonical owner; a documentation reference MUST NOT become a second owner.
MCP 2026-07-28 MUST be treated as normative only within its applicable MCP protocol-conformance domain.
Google Developer Documentation guidance MUST remain presentation guidance and MUST NOT define KIS runtime or governance semantics.
Implementation references and inferred evidence MUST NOT populate canonical KIS facts without a separately governed adoption decision.
Material used by deterministic generation MUST resolve to a reproducible revision or content hash; live moving web content MUST NOT be a silent build input.
Contradictions with a canonical owner MUST surface as diagnostics and MUST NOT silently change the canonical value.
Generated documentation MUST remain a deterministic review projection with no write-back authority.
External content MUST NOT be harvested beyond metadata or bounded evidence until licensing, attribution, and reuse constraints are recorded.
